summary:
Through coord 0.112 and the 0.113 source of #4802, one passive association kept at most 8 source cursors and 256 response identities and never removed either. A new path past 8 gave `source-index-full-capture-deferred`; a pass whose new identities would exceed 256 deferred without advancing, so every later pass rescanned and deferred again. Measured 2026-10-23 on the fdev host (capture-only, no network): two real Claude Code 2.1.309 transcripts reached 235 observations in ten passes and then stalled; the host wrote about 152 transcripts in 24 hours. Any passive producer with many files or one long session hits this.

Retiring finished state fixes the stall but moves duplicate prevention from a permanent identity index to cursors, and that is the reusable lesson: the receiver refuses a repeated identity at a revision it already holds with a different content digest (`native fact identity conflict`) and quarantines the whole batch, and passive facts carry capturedAt and sourceGeneration, so any re-read differs. Independent review found five re-read paths after retirement: a hard link, a rename, a copy under a new inode, an active file replaced by a new inode, and a hard link closing in the same pass (which also crashed on a null index entry). Each needs explicit suppression with a visible gap.

The fix (Outcome #4640, this revision): a source closes at end of descriptor on a line boundary after 15 minutes unmodified (mtime taken after the read); its cursor becomes a compact retired entry (cap 384) and its identities leave the index; an active Claude transcript keeps its newest 24 identities. Suppression: `source-alias-skipped` (inode already owned), `closed-source-discontinuity-skipped` (marked, not rescanned), `continuity-replay-suppressed` (at or before a per-source high-water timestamp after a continuity gap), `retired-response-suppressed` (4096 most recently retired identities, 16-hex prefixes) and `pre-horizon-record-suppressed` (unknown source at or before one second after the newest evicted entry's mtime). Retirement rides the existing intent, so a crash applies it once.

Drain throughput: a drain sends at most one envelope per passive chain, because later envelopes wait behind the earliest pending head, so drain must run at least as often as capture emits batches (at most 24 responses each). At 128 ready envelopes or 8 MiB, enqueue returns `spool-overload`, the intent and cursors are retained and capture stops; nothing queued is dropped.

Limits: the 24-identity window relies on observed, undocumented Claude writer ordering; a copy of an old closed file made after its identities left the recent set and before its entry is evicted can still repeat responses; records without timestamps are suppressed where a timestamp bound applies; active Codex rollouts keep the no-retirement rule; rolling a retired association back to 0.112 would re-read closed sources. Tests are synthetic; installed adoption and receiver ingestion (Host built from 61526e94 or later) are separate.
title: Passive telemetry needs bounded retirement, and retirement needs explicit suppression of every re-read path
